title: Regional failover lanes and residency-boundary controls for Private/VPC deployments
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Customers running Private/VPC deployments require strict residency guarantees with deterministic, auditable regional failover. Current behavior permits broad region fallback that can cause transient policy violations and ambiguous audit trails. Goal: introduce 'failover lanes' — explicit, policy-driven routes that define allowed destination regions, evacuation prechecks, and evidence artifacts produced on each failover action. This ticket implements control plane primitives, runtime hooks, and reporting automation to ensure every cross-region evacuation is both policy-compliant and fully auditable.
acceptance_criteria: Define a 'failover lane' CRD in the private control plane that lists ordered candidate regions and constraints (data-jurisdiction tags, maximum allowed latency, tenant-allow-list).
Runtime enforces lane membership: only target regions on the lane can be selected for automatic failover; any out-of-lane target requires manual approval recorded in audit logs.

Evacuation precheck must evaluate retention/lock state, KMS key residency, and in-flight KV cache snapshot eligibility; precheck failures block automatic failover and produce evidence artifacts explaining the block.

Automated evidence package produced for each planned and executed evacuation containing: lane version, evaluated constraints, queue snapshot, KV cache digests, KMS key IDs, and a signed control-plane decision record stored in the customer's audit bucket.

Console and API surfaces show real-time failover lane decisions, last evacuation evidence bundle link, and a machine-readable report endpoint (/v1/audit/failover/<id>) returning a signed JSON artifact.
End-to-end integration tests simulate tenant-bound residency policies and assert that only allowed lanes trigger automatic evacuation under simulated region outages.
design_notes: Failover lane model: small immutable versions. Each lane has metadata: owner project, region list with constraints, TTL for automatic eviction, and allowed exception scopes.
Control plane API: POST /v1/lanes to create, PATCH to rotate lane (creates new version), GET returns lane+version history. Each lane change emits signed event to audit stream.
Runtime hook points: pre-evacuation validator, evacuation executor, post-evacuation verifier. Implement validators as policy plugins so customers can inject custom checks in Private deployments.

Evidence packaging: use deterministic JSON packing, sign with platform key and optionally with customer KMS (if available), and upload to customer-configured S3/GCS audit bucket. Include schema v1 and sha256 checksum.
Metrics & telemetry: failover_attempts_total, failover_blocked_reasons (labels), lane_version_used, evidence_bundle_generation_latency. Export to console and Prometheus endpoint.
Security: require RBAC gating for lane creation/rotation; lane rotation must be restricted to enterprise admin roles and logged with justification field.
Backward compatibility: default lane for existing Private clusters will be a single-region lane (current behavior) so no silent policy drift for customers not opting in.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): implement control plane API and lane CRD behind feature flag in staging. Enable for internal test tenants and one low-risk customer in a dedicated staging VPC.
Phase 2 (pilot): expose lane creation UI in Console for select customers. Require manual opt-in; generate evidence bundles to a staging audit location for review by security and compliance teams.

Phase 3 (general availability): enable lanes by default for all new Private clusters. Provide migration tooling to convert existing region policies into a default lane. Documentation published and customer migrations scheduled.
Rollback plan: feature flag rollback will prevent new lanes but preserve existing lane configs; provide evacuation freeze toggle to immediately stop automatic failovers while we investigate.
Communication: RFC to customers with timeline, migration docs, and a sample evidence bundle for compliance review.
test_plan: Unit tests for lane CRD validation and versioning semantics.
Integration tests: simulate region outage and verify precheck evaluation and evidence bundle content for multiple lane configurations.
Chaos test: orchestrate partial network partition between availability zones and ensure quorum rules prevent unsafe evacuation.
Security review: run adversarial test where an attacker attempts to create a lane with out-of-jurisdiction regions and assert RBAC/approval blocks it.
End-to-end compliance test: provide signed evidence bundle to internal compliance service and assert verification passes and all required fields are present.
